Ambiguity in language ○ When water boils, its bubbles are round, but when it freezes, its crystals are 6-sided. Why isn’t frozen water round or boiling water hexagonally shaped? Aren’t H2O molecules the same in either state? ○ Bubbles are round because (...) Ice crystals are shaped in such a way because (...) The water molecules are much slower and aren’t bouncing all over the place. Gaseous H2O is much higher energy and further apart so that the regular pattern of ice doesn’t come into effect.

we use the top-5 passages as the context and a per GPU batch size of 8. We train all our model with learning rate $10^{-5}$ , weight decay of 0, and maximum sequence length of 256. We train all our models for 5000 steps and a gradient accumulation step of 5. We run the classifier models with 5 different random seeds and report the best result. All experiments were done with two Nvidia-RTX6000 GPUs (the detection subtask) or two Nvidia-A40 GPUs (the writing subtask). We use half-precision training (Micikevicius et al., 2018) when training for our detection task and gradient checkpointing from fairscale (authors, 2021), and choose the best checkpoint based on the performance on the validation set and report its test set performance. For the unified models for the writing subtask, we choose the best checkpoint that gives the best BLEU score for presupposition.
